title: On The Fly: What to watch in Snap earnings report SNAP;FB;TWTR - The Fly
text:
On The Fly: What to watch in Apple earnings report » Apple (AAPL) is scheduled…
Apple (AAPL) is scheduled to report results for the company's second quarter of fiscal year 2018 after the market close on Tuesday, May 1, with a conference call scheduled for 5:00 pm ET. What to watch for: 1. SLIDING IPHONE EXPECTATIONS: On March 16, Barclays analyst Mark Moskowitz lowered his Apple estimates after visiting suppliers in Asia, telling investors then that the "lone trouble spot is smartphones, while most other segments appear to be in good shape." He said at the time that iPhones X and 8 demand trends were "soft," with "no signs of any deferred mega cycle in making." Since then, Moskowitz reduced his estimates and price target for the second time in as many months, cutting his price target for Apple shares to $157 from $168 on concerns that a "weaker iPhone franchise" could require the company to allocate more cash to acquisitions. He also warned there could be a "sell on the news event" if capital returns are only in line with expectations. He kept an Equal Weight rating on Apple. Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty said that she expects the company to report in-line March quarter results, but she also believes that consensus estimates for its June quarter need to be lowered. The analyst, who lowered her own June quarter iPhone shipment estimate to 34M from 40.5M, believes the Q3 consensus iPhone shipment estimate could be revised "meaningfully lower." While she trimmed her Apple price target to $200 from $203, Huberty kept an Overweight rating on Apple and recommended buying any post-earnings dip. Bernstein analyst A.M. Sacconaghi Jr. sees the risk-reward going into Q2 earnings as neutral to slightly negative, and continues to believe that estimates are more likely to go down than up in the near-term. Apple's expected large capital return program could mitigate the impact, but the analyst believes the investor narrative post-earnings will likely be dominated by whether iPhone can grow over time. He reiterated a Market Perform rating and $170 price target on the shares. According to Bloomberg data, the consensus forecast is for Apple to report Q2 iPhone units of 51.4M, followed by 42.0M units in Q3. 2. RISING CAPITAL RETURN EXPECTATIONS: In recent years, the company's March quarter, or fiscal Q2, report is when it addresses its capital return plans for the year. The Financial Times recently said that analysts expect Apple to increase its shareholder returns by at least $100B as the company plans to redistribute its repatriated overseas profits. 3. NEW PHONES, NEW HEADSET?: In late March, Digitimes reported that Apple recently determined that its next-generation iPhone lineup will consist of two OLED-based devices, one being a 5.85-inch model and one being 6.45-inches, along with a 6.1-inch LCD model. Thanks to an agreement with supplier Samsung Display that will prevent cost increases from the panel side, Apple may position the new 5.85-inch OLED device as the cheapest model of all three next-generation iPhone models, Digitimes added. Looking further out for innovation, CNET said on April 27 that Apple is working on a project, codenamed T288, for a headset for both Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality that would be untethered from a computer or smartphone. Citing a source familiar with the plans, CNET added that the project is still in its early stages but is slated for release in 2020. 03/08/13
